channel.title: Nicotine Science and Policy
channel.description: Daily digest of views, debates and discussions on nicotine science, policy, regulation and advocacy.

item.title: Why New Zealand Is Getting It Right?
item.description: New Zealand’s progress shows what tobacco policy can look like when harm reduction is treated as part of the solution. Smoking has fallen alongside access to vaping, suggesting that lower-risk alternatives can help accelerate the move away from combustion when smokers are given practical options. The lesson is not that regulation should disappear, but that it should support the direction of change already reducing harm. Public health should learn from countries where smoking is falling fastest, not dismiss the tools helping make it happen. (Published on October 12, 2026bygfn.tv)

item.title: A Snapshot Is Not a Verdict
item.description: A snapshot can show where nicotine use is at one moment, but it cannot explain the whole journey. Smoking, vaping and switching are dynamic behaviours, shaped by timing, motivation, access and whether people move fully away from cigarettes. Treating one data point as a final verdict risks missing the direction of change that matters most for harm reduction. Better analysis follows the pathway, not just the photograph. (Published on October 12, 2026bysubstack.com)

item.title: The FDA’s $7 billion bureaucratic black box is fueling black markets
item.description: The FDA review backlog is not just an administrative problem; it shapes the market smokers actually face. Legal smoke-free products wait in uncertainty, while illicit and unapproved products move faster than the system designed to regulate them. That imbalance leaves adult smokers with fewer accountable options and gives the black market more space to grow. Product review should be rigorous, but it also has to be timely enough to support harm reduction in the real world. (Published on October 12, 2026bywashingtonexaminer.com)
